newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end up on rising new issues.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end up on rising new issues.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates ended higher on Wednesday in weak trading due to expectations of heavy new issues, brokers said.
"Expectations of rising new issues this week depressed sentiment," said a Daewoo Securities broker.
Brokers said new issues were estimated at 332.7 billion won on Thursday, compared with 191.8 billion today.

"Liquidity with institutions, especially banks, seem to be drying up," the Daewoo trader said. Brokers said banks appeared to be suffering from fund shortages ahead of the central bank's bi-monthly review on Saturday of banks' reserve status.
Three-month CD yields also rose in the belief that CDs were overbought. But overnight call rates closed unchanged with banks sticking to daily routine deals, they said.
